contexts.text: They offered Him gifts, gold, frankincense, and myrrh (); where gold = good; frankincense and myrrh, the things which are grateful, because from love and faith; and which are therefore called the praises of Jehovah ().
Things celestial and the derivative spiritual things are meant by gold and frankincense ().
Gold, frankincense, and myrrh = celestial, spiritual, and natural good.
Sheba = Knowledges and adorations, which are frankincense and calamus ().

Fine flour with oil and frankincense (in the meat-offering, ) represented all things of charity; fine flour, what is spiritual thereof; oil, what is celestial; and frankincense, what is on this account grateful.
Frankincense, from its odour, = what is grateful and acceptable.
Gold and frankincense () = goods and truths, which are the praises of Jehovah.
The doctrinal things of good are gold; the doctrinal things of truth are frankincense; both are the praises of Jehovah.
Gold () = celestial love; frankincense, spiritual love; myrrh, these loves in the Natural.
By cinnamon, incenses, ointments, and frankincense () are signified truths which are from good; but with them, truths perverted and falsities from evil.

By gold, frankincense, and myrrh are signified all things which belong to the good of love and of faith directed to the Lord; gold, the things of the good of love; frankincense, the things of the good of faith; and myrrh, the things belonging to both in externals... (The wise men knew from correspondences) that gold, frankincense, and myrrh signified the goods which are to be offered to God.
The pure frankincense which was to be put upon the cakes () = truth from celestial good, which is the ultimate or outermost of the Celestial Kingdom.

The reason no oil and frankincense were to be put upon the meat-offering of the sacrifice for sin and guilt, was that by oil is signified the good of love, and by frankincense the truth of that good; and by the sacrifice for sin and guilt is signified purification and expiation from evils and the derivative falsities, which were not to be commingled with good and the derivative truth. AC 10177:12.

Frankincense, specifically, = the truth of faith; and therefore when frankincense is mentioned in the Word, there is adjoined oil, bread, meat-offering, or gold, by which is signified the good of love. Illustrated.
As the good of love is not possible except together with the truth of faith... upon every meat-offering there was frankincense; and also upon the breads of faces ().
Gold () = good; frankincense, internal truth; and myrrh, external truth, both from good... Frankincense is mentioned in the second place, because it = the internal truth which is from good.
By frankincense is signified internal truth in the internal man, which is spiritual good.

Pure frankincense () = inmost truth, which is spiritual good; (for) frankincense = that which is purified from the falsity of evil... The good with those who are in the Spiritual Kingdom is nothing but truth, which is called good when a man wills and does it from conscience and affection.

As frankincense = spiritual good, and good is what reigns in all truths, disposes them, conjoins them, and gives affection to them, therefore frankincense is mentioned in the last place; and therefore it was from it that the vessels of incense were called censers; for the name is given from the essential, which is good.
It is called pure frankincense, because pure = purified from the falsities of evil.
Pure frankincense = spiritual good.
Gold = celestial good; frankincense, spiritual good; and myrrh, natural good; from which three is all worship. AR 277:end. AE 324:10. AE 491:5.
Frankincense has a similar signification to incense, because frankincense was the principal spice from which the incense was made.

And cinnamon, and incenses, and ointment, and frankincense () = that they no longer have worship from spiritual goods and truths, because they have nothing internally in their worship which corresponds to the things here named.
The essential of the incense-offerings is meant by the frankincense.
By the gold and frankincense which they shall carry () are meant goods and truths from good, which, from being such, are grateful.

As spiritual good, which is the good of charity towards the neighbour, derives its essence and its soul from celestial good, which is the good of love to the Lord, therefore frankincense, by which is signified spiritual good, was put upon the breads of faces, by which is signified celestial good.
That incense and frankincense = spiritual good; and the incense-offering, the worship which is grateful from this good. Illustrated.

By the gold and frankincense which they shall carry, is signified worship from the spiritual good which is from celestial good; gold = celestial good, and frankincense, spiritual good; and because worship from these is signified, it is said and they shall proclaim the praises of Jehovah.
As the meat-offering = the good of celestial love, and frankincense the good of spiritual love, oil and frankincense were put upon the meat-offering of fine flour...

The frankincense was the primary thing (of the incense), and the other three spices were added for the gratefulness of their odour... From this it is evident why frankincense = the same as the compounded incense, namely, spiritual good.
To offer frankincense and bless vanity () = to worship God from such things as represent spiritual good, and yet to love evil and falsity...

To bring burnt-offering, sacrifice, meat-offering, and frankincense () = worship from celestial good and from spiritual good in the natural man; burnt-offering = worship from celestial good; sacrifice, worship from spiritual good; meat-offering and frankincense, good and the truth of good in the natural man.
That frankincense, in the Word, = spiritual good; and in like manner the censer which was its containant. Illustrated.

I have not made thee to serve by a meat-offering, nor wearied thee by frankincense (). Meat-offering and frankincense are mentioned, because by the meat-offering, which was from fine flour, and thus was bread, is signified celestial good; and therefore by frankincense is signified spiritual good.

Oil was poured upon the meat-offering, and frankincense was put on it; and this in order that by the meat-offering there might be represented the conjunction of celestial good and spiritual good; for oil = celestial good, and frankincense spiritual good.

Therefore, also, frankincense was put upon the breads of faces in the tabernacle; and this also for the sake of the conjunction of both goods; for the breads = celestial good, and the frankincense, spiritual good...

The incense-offerings represented worship from spiritual good; and frankincense = this good... thus by the incense-offerings from frankincense was represented the things which thence proceed; and the things which proceed from that good are truths; for this good thinks them and speaks them... Moreover, spiritual good is formed in man by means of truths...

The reason the smoke of the incense-offerings = truths from spiritual good, is that the frankincense, from which came the smoke, = spiritual good; and the fire by which the frankincense was kindled, celestial good.

And ointment and frankincense ( 3) = profaned worship from spiritual love. Ointment = the good of spiritual love; and frankincense = the truth of spiritual good. The reason it is spiritual love which is signified by ointment and frankincense, is that the incense-offerings were effected by means of them...
Statements of Scripture by which Truths are confirmed ascend into Heaven; they are like the smoke from frankincense.
